enade-2008-computing-d10.notes: RESOLVED IN PHASE 3K (wrong_column_order): the reading-order scramble documented since Phase 3E/3G is root-caused precisely. D10's own page 7 genuinely changes column topology three times: a photo beside a two-column newspaper article (top), full-width single-column prose for two more motivating fragments (middle), and a genuine two-column bulleted 'Observações' box (bottom). layout.detect_column_margins makes exactly one (left_margin=35, right_margin=250) decision for the whole page, and the pre-existing extract_page_lines applies it globally - every line at or past x0=245 sorts after every line before it, regardless of where on the page either actually sits. That scrambles the collage: the entire right-side newspaper article and the entire right half of the bulleted box get pushed to after every left-side line, including the page's own closing full-width paragraphs. Fixed via a new module, reading_zones.py (zoned_reading_order): a vertical window is only treated as genuinely two-column when both sides have real, substantial evidence concurrently occupying that specific window (never merely because a line's own x0 sits past the page-wide right margin) - this correctly leaves the photo-caption zone (one lone citation on the 'left' side, no real column there) and the closing full-width paragraphs (zero 'right'-side content at all) as ordinary y0-sorted flow, while still correctly interleaving the one window that is genuinely two columns (the bulleted box, three substantial lines on each side). Re-inspected against page 7's own raw text: a full word-set comparison (478 words each side) confirms zero words missing, zero words added; each of the three newspaper articles' own headline, body and citation now read in one continuous, correct sequence, followed by the actual task prompt and the fully-interleaved Observações bullets ending on the correct closing value line. One residual, cosmetic-only limitation: all three articles' own text is still rendered as a single merged paragraph rather than being split at each article's own boundary (the paragraph-merge heuristic in assembler._build_statement_segments is gap-based, not topology-aware, and was not changed this phase) - this affects readability, not content accuracy or sequence. Activated only for this one page via a hash-locked layout override (data/manifests/layout-overrides.yaml, force_zoned_reading_order_page) on top of the booklet-level zoned_reading_order_gate - applying the new mechanism to every two-column page in 2008-b was tried and reverted after it regressed several already-correct pages (Q28, Q63, Q71 among others), because extract_page_lines's own output order feeds other order-dependent heuristics (figures.py's own label-absorption) tuned against the old, page-wide split. Confirmed by full regeneration: only enade-2008-computing-d10.md changed in 2008-b; zero 2011/2021 drift; reproducibility confirmed (two independent runs byte-identical).
